pr_title: logging: fixes and enhancements to initialization and shell cmds
pr_body:
## logging: init backend id regardless of autostart

The `id` is basically a compile-time constant. Setting it every
time the backend is enabled is unnecessary. Instead, set it on
`z_log_init()` regardless of whether or not it requires to be
`autostart`ed.

Fixes an issue where the `filter_get`/`filter_set`
accessed the wrong index and displayed the wrong log level when
user accesses the status of an uninitialized backend via:
`log backend <uninitialized_backend> status`.

Also fixes an issue when user tries to list the backends via:
`log list_backends`, where all uninitialized backends will have
ID = 0.


## logging: log_cmds: init uninitialized backend on `log_go()`

For backends that do not autostart themselves, initialize
& enable them on `log backend <log_backend_*> go`, so
that they function properly.

Fixes #84952
Fixes #84954

issue_context.title: logging: log_cmds: provide a mean to initialize backends from shell
issue_context.body:
**Is your enhancement proposal related to a problem? Please describe.**
For backends that are not autostarted by the logging subsys, while they can be interacted via the shell cmd interface, they must be initialized manually by the user applications or else they will not work properly.

No error is thrown by the shell cmd interface when a user interacted with an uninitialized log backend, causing confusion.

**Describe the solution you'd like**
Provide a mean for user to initialize backends interactively from shell cmd interface.

**Describe alternatives you've considered**
Keep the current behavior, but throw error when user is trying to configure a backend that hasn't been initialized.

**Additional context**
See also #84952, this issue exists in v3.7 and earlier versions

review_comments: This is similar to how the logging subsys initializes the backends with `autostart` set, but potentially livelocking the shell backend thread.
